correctness.rationale: The zero-mean bounded real/complex norm reduces to choosing four largest of eight product-kernel masses; log-likelihood signs yield the exact majority and dictator branches. The integral for J(u) has strictly negative logarithmic derivative, so the ratio h(r_it)/h(r_1t) is strictly decreasing for all r_i>r_1 and gives a unique transverse crossing. Taylor expansion and mode rigidity establish the remaining scope. Standalone exact arithmetic exhausts 70 balanced candidates for 343 rational multiplier triples, with additional direct semigroup checks; the proof is infinite in parameters and does not rely on the finite tests.

value.rationale: Exact finite-time norm and norming-mode classification reveals a genuine nonsmoothness of an operator norm along an analytic centered heat semigroup. The strictly unique majority-to-dictator transition depends on rate multiplicity, with sharp onset and exact final exponential decay. The phenomenon distinguishes transient collective mixing from terminal single-eigenmode domination and is not a routine evaluation of one fixed test function.
